
{{alias}}( N, x, strideX, y, strideY )
    Computes the integral of a double-precision floating-point strided array
    using the trapezoidal rule.

    The `N` and stride parameters determine which elements in the strided arrays
    are accessed at runtime.

    Indexing is relative to the first index. To introduce an offset, use a typed
    array view.

    If `N <= 1`, the function returns `0.0`.

    The function computes an approximation of the integral using the trapezoidal
    rule whose accuracy depends on the sample point spacing and the smoothness
    of the underlying function.

    Parameters
    ----------
    N: integer
        Number of indexed elements.

    x: Float64Array
        First input array.

    strideX: integer
        Stride length for `x`.

    y: Float64Array
        Second input array.

    strideY: integer
        Stride length for `y`.

    Returns
    -------
    out: number
        Integral approximation.

    Examples
    --------
    // Standard usage:
    > var x = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 ] );
    > var y = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 0.0, 1.0, 4.0, 9.0 ] );
    > var out = {{alias}}( x.length, x, 1, y, 1 )
    9.5

    // Using `N` and stride parameters:
    > x = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 0.0, -1.0, 1.0, -1.0, 2.0 ] );
    > y = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 0.0, 2.0, 6.0 ] );
    > out = {{alias}}( 3, x, 2, y, 1 )
    5.0

    // Using view offsets:
    > x = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0, 2.0 ] );
    > y = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ -1.0, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 4.0 ] );
    > var x1 = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( x.buffer, x.BYTES_PER_ELEMENT*1 );
    > var y1 = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( y.buffer, y.BYTES_PER_ELEMENT*3 );
    > out = {{alias}}( 3, x1, 2, y1, 1 )
    3.5


{{alias}}.ndarray( N, x, strideX, offsetX, y, strideY, offsetY )
    Computes the integral of a double-precision floating-point strided array
    using the trapezoidal rule and alternative indexing semantics.

    While typed array views mandate a view offset based on the underlying
    buffer, the offset parameters support indexing based on a starting index.

    Parameters
    ----------
    N: integer
        Number of indexed elements.

    x: Float64Array
        First input array.

    strideX: integer
        Stride length for `x`.

    offsetX: integer
        Starting index for `x`.

    y: Float64Array
        Second input array.

    strideY: integer
        Stride length for `y`.

    offsetY: integer
        Starting index for `y`.

    Returns
    -------
    out: number
        Integral approximation.

    Examples
    --------
    // Standard usage:
    > var x = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 ] );
    > var y = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 0.0, 1.0, 4.0, 9.0 ] );
    > var out = {{alias}}.ndarray( x.length, x, 1, 0, y, 1, 0 )
    9.5

    // Advanced indexing:
    > x = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0, 2.0 ] );
    > y = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ -1.0, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 4.0 ] );
    > out = {{alias}}.ndarray( 3, x, 2, 1, y, 1, 3 )
    3.5

    See Also
    --------
